hints: Look at Period 3 structure and bonding, since melting point and conductivity both depend on whether the element is metallic, giant covalent or simple molecular.
Remember that melting point rises to a peak at silicon due to its giant covalent lattice, then falls sharply, while conductivity falls steadily from metals to non-metals.
Test each set by asking if the same one element is top for melting and bottom for conducting, and keep the set where those two titles meet.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two Period 3 trends**

Think like a teacher with you. Melting point is about strength of lattice. Conductivity is about mobile electrons.

Metals ($\text{Na}$, $\text{Mg}$, $\text{Al}$) conduct well. Giant covalent $\text{Si}$ is a semiconductor. Non-metals ($\text{P}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Cl}$) are insulators.

**Fix the melting point pattern**

Melting point increases from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Al}$ with stronger metallic bonding, then jumps to a maximum at $\text{Si}$.

$$\text{Si (giant covalent, many strong Si-Si bonds) >> Al > Mg > Na >> P, S, Cl (weak van der Waals)}$$

**Fix the conductivity pattern**

Conductivity is highest for metals and then drops. $\text{Si}$ conducts only a little, and $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Cl}$ essentially do not conduct.

$$\text{conductivity: Na, Mg, Al (high) > Si (very low) > P, S, Cl (zero)}$$

**Find the set where one element does both**

We need the highest melting element in the set to also be the poorest conductor in that set.

Only in $\text{Mg}$, $\text{Al}$, $\text{Si}$ does $\text{Si}$ win on both counts: highest melting point and lowest conductivity.

options.A: In magnesium, aluminium and silicon, silicon has the highest melting point (giant covalent lattice with strong covalent bonds throughout) and the lowest conductivity (semiconductor, no sea of delocalised electrons like Mg and Al). One single element, Si, holds both titles, so this fits perfectly.
options.B: In aluminium, silicon and phosphorus, silicon still has the highest melting point, but phosphorus has the lowest conductivity because it is a simple molecular insulator. The two titles belong to two different elements, so the word both fails.
options.C: In sodium, magnesium and aluminium, all three are metals with good conductivity and relatively similar melting points. Aluminium has the highest melting point but sodium has the lowest conductivity, so again no single element has both properties.
options.D: In silicon, phosphorus and chlorine, silicon has the highest melting point, but silicon is a semiconductor and conducts slightly better than phosphorus and chlorine, which are both insulators. Silicon is top for melting but not bottom for conducting, so this set fails.
